channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan's Communications Service monitors telecom issues in Gorno-Badakhshan
item.description: Tajikistan's Communications Service is monitoring the quality of mobile and internet services in cities and districts, particularly in remote Gorno-Badakhshan regions. Working groups are assessing network infrastructure, user satisfaction, and identifying technical problems to improve service quality for residents.

item.title: Suspect arrested in Bishkek with 1.5 kilograms of synthetic drugs
item.description: A man born in 1989 was apprehended in Bishkek on suspicion of distributing drugs through 'hidden locations'. Law enforcement officers found 1.5 kilograms of synthetic drug 'Alpha-PVP' and 4 grams of hashish at his residence during a search.

item.title: Urals Oil Prices Surpass $110 Per Barrel Amid Supply Concerns
item.description: Russian Urals crude oil prices have exceeded $110 per barrel, reaching their highest level since April. This surge is attributed to concerns over Middle Eastern supply disruptions and reduced availability from Gulf producers. Fuel premiums for Indian ports also rose significantly.

item.title: 1.5 Kilograms of Synthetic Drugs Confiscated from Man in Bishkek
item.description: A 37-year-old man was detained in Bishkek on suspicion of drug distribution via dead drops. Authorities seized 1.5 kilograms of Alpha-PVP and 4 grams of hashish from his residence. Investigations are ongoing to identify other potential individuals involved in the illicit drug trade.

item.title: Uzbek man who fought for Russia in Ukraine sentenced to 3 years
item.description: A 25-year-old Uzbek citizen, R.B., who fought for Russia in the Ukraine conflict, has been sentenced to three years in prison by a court in Fergana region. He signed a contract with the Russian Armed Forces in November 2023, participated in combat operations in Luhansk, and was injured by a drone in April 2024.

item.title: Tajikistan and MCDF discuss investment projects for infrastructure and regional connectivity
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Minister of Economic Development met with the Director General of the Multilateral Cooperation Center for Development Finance (MCDF) to discuss strengthening cooperation and implementing priority investment projects. Discussions focused on quality infrastructure, regional ties, green economy, renewable energy, and climate adaptation. Both sides expressed readiness to expand trade and attract investments.

item.title: French Interior Ministry Representative Begins Work in Tashkent to Coordinate Regional Law Enforcement Cooperation
item.description: Cyril Gu, the representative of the French Ministry of Interior, has started his activities in Tashkent. He will be responsible for coordinating cooperation between law enforcement agencies of Central Asian countries.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Visit Karakalpakstan for Two-Day Trip
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit the Republic of Karakalpakstan for a two-day trip. During the visit, he will review projects in industry, agriculture, education, healthcare, transport, tourism, and sports, focusing on employment and community development.

item.title: Waste-to-Energy Plant Producing 110 Million kWh to Be Built in Jizzakh Region, Uzbekistan
item.description: Measures have been defined to implement an investment project in Jizzakh and Sirdaryo regions to improve the ecological situation and generate electricity through waste processing. The project will be carried out by a consortium of Chinese companies, with an investment agreement signed for 30 years.

item.title: Uzbek youth may find employment in Japan through targeted training programs
item.description: Uzbek youth may be employed in Japan as plans are underway to expand employment opportunities through targeted vocational and language training. This initiative aims to facilitate future employment for young Uzbek citizens in the Japanese labor market. Further details are available on Daryo.uz.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Approves New Date for Presidential Elections
item.description: The Jogorku Kenesh, Kyrgyzstan's parliament, has amended its regulations to set a new date for presidential elections. The vote will now occur on the fourth Wednesday of January, instead of the third Sunday in October. President Sadyr Japarov signed the amendment, aligning the parliamentary regulations with the constitutional election law.

item.title: Bishkek Waste Processing Plant's Performance Assessed by Commission
item.description: A commission, including specialists from the Ministry of Natural Resources, Ecology, and Technical Supervision, evaluated the Bishkek waste processing plant that generates electricity. The commission inspected the landfill and the plant's operations. Plans include a second phase to increase processing capacity to 3,000 tons of waste daily.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Iraq Discuss Agreement on International Road Transport
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Iraq are working towards an agreement on international road transport, as discussed by Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Minister of Transport and Iraq's Chargé d'Affaires. Kyrgyzstan has drafted an agreement, aiming to facilitate transport routes via Central Asian countries and address visa issues for freight carriers.

item.title: Jizzakh to generate electricity from solid waste incineration
item.description: A project in Jizzakh will produce electricity by incinerating solid municipal waste. The project company will provide an $8 million bank guarantee to ensure its obligations during construction.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan National Bank reports on currency exchange rates
item.description: The Kazakh tenge and Russian ruble strengthened, reaching yearly and monthly highs. The euro and Chinese yuan depreciated, while the US dollar remained unchanged. The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan intervened by selling $220.7 million in dollars on September 6.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and US National Guard discuss cultural and youth cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Minister of Culture met with the U.S. Montana National Guard to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation. Areas of focus include youth policy, education, sports, arts, and cinema, with potential for hosting cultural and film days.

item.title: Energy from waste: How South Korea solved its food waste problem
item.description: South Korea has largely eliminated household food waste from landfills by converting it into energy. New York is currently testing this approach. The article discusses the methods used and the success of this initiative.

item.title: Drone Strike Occurs Near Polish-Ukrainian Border, Warsaw on Alert
item.description: A drone strike occurred in Ukraine's Volyn region, approximately 4 km from the Polish border, on September 17. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated the explosion happened near Dorohusk, likely targeting a gas station. Polish fighter jets were scrambled, and airports in Lublin and Rzeszow temporarily suspended operations.

item.title: EU Ambassador: Democracy is Never a Finished Product, Faces Modern Challenges
item.description: The EU Ambassador to Uzbekistan stated that democracy is fundamentally the people's power, allowing citizens to choose and replace leaders. He acknowledged the growing appeal of authoritarian models but believes people ultimately desire democratic choice, even when seeking stronger leaders. Democracy, he argued, is our natural state and inherent desire.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Launch New Agricultural Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea are initiating new projects focused on agricultural innovation, investment, and training. Agreements include establishing a joint working group, developing grant projects for water-saving technologies and soil fertility, and adapting agriculture to climate change.

item.title: Samarkand hosts record-breaking 46th World Chess Olympiad
item.description: The 46th World Chess Olympiad has begun in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, with a record number of participants. Over 200 countries and nearly 2000 players are competing in 11 rounds. The opening ceremony featured a drone show, 3D mapping, and fireworks. Uzbekistan's team, seeded third, secured six victories in the first round.

item.title: Azerbaijan prioritizes Turkic world cooperation, says President Aliyev
item.description: President Ilham Aliyev stated that Azerbaijan views the Turkic world as a key foreign policy priority, focusing on expanding economic and investment cooperation. He noted joint investment funds with Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan, aiming to strengthen economic ties and enhance the role of the Organization of Turkic States internationally.

item.title: Saudi Arabia asks China to pressure Iran and Houthis over Yemen conflict
item.description: Saudi Arabia has requested China to exert pressure on Iran and the Houthis regarding their military activities in Yemen. Following this appeal, Beijing reportedly contacted Tehran, urging them to halt the Houthi actions. The report cites sources in Riyadh.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Iraq to sign agreement on international road transport
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has prepared a draft agreement on international road transport for Iraq's review, aiming to establish a regulatory framework. The countries also discussed expanding transport routes via Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, and Iran, and improving visa procedures for international truck drivers.

item.title: Uzbekistan to reform film industry, empowering private studios and independent creators
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva announced a shift in Uzbekistan's film industry, with the state becoming a strategic partner rather than a direct commissioner. Private studios and independent creators will drive the industry, while the state will focus on financial support and development. The system for film production, distribution, and export will be modernized.

item.title: Uzbekistan Recognized by UN-Water for Significant Water Conservation Achievements
item.description: Uzbekistan has been recognized by UN-Water for its substantial progress in water conservation. Over eight months, the country saved 9.457 billion cubic meters of water through the implementation of water-saving and digital technologies, irrigation, and land laser leveling. The goal is to save 11 billion cubic meters by year-end.

item.title: US Congress Approves "Satanic Sanctions" Against Russia, Awaiting Trump's Signature
item.description: The US Congress has definitively passed a bill imposing "hellish sanctions" on Russia over the war in Ukraine and sent it to President Donald Trump for signature. Experts suggest four main reasons why Trump may delay implementing these sanctions.

item.title: UN Resident Coordinator in Kyrgyzstan Receives Government Certificate of Honor
item.description: Adylbek Kasymaliev met with UN Resident Coordinator Antje Grave upon completion of her mission in Kyrgyzstan. They discussed cooperation and future prospects. Kasymaliev presented Grave with a Certificate of Honor for her contributions to strengthening partnership between the UN and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Central Asian Civil Society Forum Discusses Democratic Development in Samarkand
item.description: A Central Asian forum on civil society's role in democratic development is underway in Samarkand, gathering around 200 specialists from Uzbekistan and international organizations. Participants are discussing democratic trends, challenges, and future directions based on Uzbekistan's and Central Asia's experiences.

item.title: US sentences Afghan militant linked to Crocus City Hall attack to 20 years
item.description: A US court has sentenced an Afghan militant, Mohammad Sharifulah, to 20 years in prison for his involvement in terrorist attacks, including providing instructions to the perpetrators of the Crocus City Hall attack. The US Justice Department stated he was a key link in ISIS-K operations and participated in over ten attacks since 2016.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes separate licensing for telecom operators and radio spectrum allocation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Digital Development proposes to regulate telecom operator licensing and radio frequency spectrum allocation separately. The draft resolution, open for public discussion, aims to simplify procedures and create equal conditions. Currently, both are covered by a single regulation from 2017.

item.title: Tajikistan's parliament discusses withdrawal from the International Criminal Court
item.description: Tajikistan's lower house of parliament discussed a draft resolution on terminating its participation in the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (ICC). Details of the decision were not provided. Tajikistan signed and ratified the statute in 1998 and 2000 respectively.

item.title: Pashinyan: Armenia Open to CSTO Exit if Proposed, Russian Base Decision is Moscow's
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan stated that if there are proposals to remove Armenia from the CSTO, they are welcome. He also commented on the Russian military base in Armenia, asserting that the decision to keep or withdraw it rests with Moscow. Pashinyan indicated no need for threats regarding these matters.

item.title: Chinese Defense Minister Calls for Joint Efforts to Protect Peace and Stability
item.description: Chinese Defense Minister Dong Jun urged joint efforts to safeguard international and regional stability, foster a favorable security environment, and ensure peaceful development. Speaking at the 13th Xiangshan Forum in Beijing, he met with defense ministers from Thailand, Mongolia, Cambodia, and Singapore. The forum's theme is "Forging Consensus on Stability, Promoting Security Governance."

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Develop 300 Preschool Education Materials by 2029
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Education plans to develop 300 innovative, competency-based materials for preschool education by 2029. These materials, supported by the Islamic Development Bank and other partners, will be available in print and digital formats to aid child development.

item.title: Uzbekistan to offer preferential loans up to $5 million for electrotechnical firms
item.description: Uzbekistan will provide preferential loans of up to $5 million to electrotechnical companies. Loans will have a term of up to two years with a three-month grace period and an annual interest rate of 6%. Key investors will be exempt from property and profit taxes for 10 years.

item.title: Montana National Guard delegation discusses cooperation with Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Minister of Culture met with a delegation from the Montana National Guard to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation. Key areas of focus included youth policy, education, sports, culture, and cinematography. Both sides expressed interest in youth exchange programs and potential "Montana Days" of culture and film in Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Kyrgyz State Security Committee uncovers financial violations in Naryn region
item.description: The State Committee for National Security of Kyrgyzstan has uncovered financial violations by officials in the Naryn region related to pasture land fees. Funds collected from locals for pasture use were not fully remitted to the local budget. The financial damage is estimated at over 36 million soms.

item.title: Kushoniyon District Sees Major Upgrades for Early Childhood Development
item.description: Kushoniyon District has renovated health and educational facilities and established new early childhood development centers as part of the 'Early Childhood Development for Human Capital Growth in Tajikistan' project. Six primary healthcare facilities were repaired, one new health center built, and a modern preschool prototype created.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Dollar Exchange Rate Rises for Third Consecutive Day
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has increased for the third consecutive day. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan announced the exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective September 18. The announcement details the new values for various foreign currencies.
